samples.summary: Vacuous guard: `yml.indexOf(...)` returning -1 makes `step` the last character, so the "promote job must still invoke mark-ready" assertion can never fire
samples.evidence: `const step = yml.slice(yml.indexOf("node ./scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs"));` — when the substring is absent, `indexOf` returns -1 and `String.prototype.slice(-1)` returns the final character of the YAML, so `assert.ok(step.length > 0, "the promote job must still invoke mark-ready.mjs")` on the next line passes with a 1-char string. The intended failure mode (invocation removed/renamed) is only caught incidentally by the later regex assertions, and the message that would be printed points at the wrong cause. Should be `const at = yml.indexOf(...); assert.notEqual(at, -1, ...)`.

samples.summary: The "no exit code outside {0,1,2,3}" scan only sees literal `process.exit(<digits>)`; the script's real fifth outcome — an uncaught exception, which exits 1 — is unpinned and is mis-read by the workflow as "gates not satisfied, leaving as draft"
samples.evidence: `SOURCE.matchAll(/process\.exit\((\d+)\)/g)` cannot observe (a) the implicit exit-0 fall-through at mark-ready.mjs:266, (b) a future `process.exit(code)` / `process.exitCode = n`, or (c) node's exit code 1 on an uncaught throw. (c) is a live path: `reviewChecks` only wraps the `ghJson` call (mark-ready.mjs:151-154), so a non-array `check_runs` payload makes `checkPassed`'s `.filter` throw outside any try, and `computeLabelSet` throws on an unknown state. Any such throw exits 1, and agent-review-panel.yml:1399 turns 1 into `echo "Not all ready-gates satisfied; leaving as draft."` with a SUCCEEDING job — exactly the silent-forever-draft failure this test file says it exists to prevent. A test that runs the CLI with a malformed check-runs payload (or asserts the tooling-error path is used for it) would pin it.
searchedFor: read scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs end to end for every exit site
grep 'process\.exit|GH_MUTATION_TOKEN|allow-no-checks' in .trusted/scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs to confirm the script is unchanged
grep mark-ready across the repo for other consumers of its exit status

samples.summary: The stub's call log is newline-delimited but the hand-off comment body contains newlines, so `calls` entries are not 1:1 with `gh` invocations
samples.evidence: `appendFileSync(process.env.GH_STUB_LOG, joined + "\n")` writes the joined argv, and `run()` does `readFileSync(logPath,"utf8").split("\n")`. `gh pr comment 7 --body <handoff>` carries a 15-line body (mark-ready.mjs:242-256), so one invocation becomes ~15 log entries. Today no fragment starts with `pr ready`/`api -X PUT`/`pr comment`, so the current assertions are accidentally correct — but `calls.length`, `deepEqual(calls, [])`, and any future prefix assertion are silently unreliable. A NUL/JSON-per-line separator (or `JSON.stringify(argv)`) would make the log unambiguous.

samples.summary: The stub `gh` resolves its interpreter through `#!/usr/bin/env node` rather than `process.execPath`, so on a runner where node is not on PATH every `gh` call fails and some tests pass for the wrong reason
samples.evidence: `const STUB_GH = `#!/usr/bin/env node ...`` combined with `PATH: ${dir}${delimiter}${process.env.PATH}`. If `node` is absent from the inherited PATH (invoked by absolute path, or a wrapper that unsets it), execFileSync("gh") fails for every call — which happens to be the expected outcome of the `fail: ["pr view"]` exit-2 test, so that test would pass while proving nothing. Writing the stub with `#!${process.execPath}` removes the dependency. Same class of fragility as the `endsWith("--json labels")` disambiguation at line 55, which silently returns the wrong shape if mark-ready ever reorders its `--json` field list.

samples.summary: Every `run()` call leaks its `mkdtempSync` directory; the suite makes ~20 per execution and never removes them
samples.evidence: `const dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "mark-ready-"));` with no `rmSync(dir, { recursive: true })` on any path (there is no `t.after`/`finally` in the file). Harmless per run, but it accumulates under TMPDIR across local iterations.
